newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Mill owners see Karachi flour shortage worsening.
newsitem.headline: Mill owners see Karachi flour shortage worsening.

text.p: A flour shortage that has sparked riots in several Pakistani cities this month is now worsening in Karachi, an industry body said on Wednesday.
The Pakistan Flour Mills Association urged the government to organise immediate supplies of wheat for Pakistan's biggest city, which has so far escaped the worst of the crisis.
"The flour shortage crisis in Karachi will worsen in the next two or three days as the flour mills have run out of wheat," Ali Mohammad, secretary of the association, told Reuters.
Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's government blames the previous caretaker administration for failing to arrange timely wheat imports.

On Tuesday, an angry mob looted more than 650 10-kg (22-lb) bags of wheat flour from the Indus Flour Mills in Karachi's District East. Police and paramilitary rangers were called in to disperse crowds at several other mills.
Witnesses said most shops had run out of wheat-flour and people were trying to buy it straight from the mills.
"People are getting panicky because of the shortage and we have decided to sell flour directly from the mills to the citizens to avoid unpleasant incidents," Mohammad said.

He said wheat consumption in the southern port city of Karachi, which has a population estimated at 12 million, was around 100,000 tonnes a month, of which 40,000 to 45,000 was supplied by the government and the rest from the open market.

"There would have been little wheat shortage if the government had not banned inter-district movement of wheat. We demand immediate lifting of this ban if the government does not arrange for immediate supplies," he said.
The association demanded that the government allocate 20,000 tonnes of wheat for Karachi out of 45,000 tonnes it imported recently for distribution to other parts of the country.
Pakistan imported 1.8 million tonnes of wheat in July-March 1996/97 compared with 1.5 million in the year-ago period.
A government official said Pakistan would receive 472,500 tonnes of wheat by mid-May and had no plans for more imports.
